payload.title: Over the Pass
paragraphs: The Captain is beaten, for now, and the white caravan is yours. Behind it the moors are grey with rain, and Saltmoss will be made to pay the tithe you took.

Ahead, the pilgrim road climbs out of the moors: stone stairs up night gorges, and paper lanterns no one has lit in a long time. Past the pass lies red country, where pieces of the sky have come down and the Ember wait.
The orbs fight for your crew, and a dead lantern burns in your hand. No one on the moors could say why. Someone on the road might.

payload.title: The Grounded Arks
paragraphs: The mural on the pilgrim road showed a sky with the Moon alone in it. You knew that sky, and could not say how.
In the Shardfall the crew learned what the red horns are: the Manalith's shell, shed as it comes closer, and some of it not shell at all. The Choir digs it out. The Ember pray for the rest to follow.
Now the road drops into a gold-hazed fen where great hulls lie broken among the reeds, a long way from any sea. Nobody has opened them in twelve hundred years. Nobody has tried with you there.

payload.title: Where the Beams Go
paragraphs: The Arks were Halcyon's, and Halcyon tried to run in them. The tide that night threw them here, and most of the people aboard never left.
You remember the boarding orders. You remember that you were not on a ship. And the door that opened for you has been noticed: the Choir is no longer chasing a stolen caravan. It is hunting you.

North, colossal arches stand over pink-lit snow, their chains humming in the cold. Past them is the white dome where you woke. The crew have never asked where you came from. Soon they will not need to.

payload.title: The Spire Stair
paragraphs: The Anchors hold nothing up. They are taps, and every draw down their lines pulls the Manalith a little closer.

Under the white dome of the Still the crew found where the tithe goes: tanks of it, far more than any Lullaby needs. They found the tank you woke in, too. The colour that brought you back was taken from people like the ones who stole the caravan with you.

Above Halcyon's dead city the Choir's spire climbs into a pink sky. At the top waits the Hierarch, and whatever all that tithe is for. Nobody in the crew asks you to pay it back. They just keep walking beside you.

payload.title: What Came Down
paragraphs: The Hierarch is gone and the organ is broken. No one drinks the skim now. But above the empty spire the Manalith hangs where it hung, beside the Moon, and it is still coming.
Halcyon stopped it, fed it and ran from it, and you helped. Everything the crew have learned of it since the moors has been hunger: the tithe, the taps, the pull.

Past the Choir's fallen pillars lies country the Choir stopped watching, where pieces of the Manalith came down and red blossom grows over the white stone. The crew want to see what grows there. You go with them.

payload.title: Claimants to the Spire
paragraphs: In the Bloom the crew found what the Manalith leaves where it lands: moss and red blossom, beasts come back changed, and the Wild living among them. Not everything that came down is hungry.
It was the first place you have stood where your being alive cost no one. The Red Seal's last warden tried to burn it anyway, and failed.

Now word of the empty spire has reached every road. The Free Holds have walled themselves up, and the Captain is still collecting. Under the spire the Underspire's neon still burns on Halcyon's taps, and the Arkgrave is filling with water.
Everyone wants the spire. And everyone who wants it asks the same question about you: what is the Commander worth?

payload.title: The March on the Anchors
paragraphs: The Captain lost the holds, and the Herd Boss lost the markets under the spire. In the flooded Arkgrave the Swamp Mistress rose with the tide one more time.
Every claimant wanted the same thing in the end, and it was not the spire. It was you. The Choir wanted Halcyon's key. Now everyone does.
Out of the deep Shardfall, where the shell is still breaking, the Ember are marching. The whole red host is headed for the Anchors, to open every tap at once and drag the Manalith down.
Whoever reaches the arches first decides how close the sky comes.

payload.title: Morrow Holds
paragraphs: Under the arches the Watch's last captain lowered his blade and gave the Anchors back to a commander of Halcyon. The chains answer you now. Only Halcyon's mana can open or close them, and yours is the last of it.
The Ember did not get their taps. The Anchors hold, and the Manalith hangs as low as it ever has, and no lower.

Past the last arch lies Morrow's Shadow: cracked plains, rock floating loose in the air, and a sky the Manalith fills, its crystals close enough to count. Beside it the Moon is a small, steady disc, the same as it has always been.
Somewhere in that dark the Demon Lord is calling the Manalith down. Past him waits a choice that only you can make. Around the fire, the crew have already started telling you what they would keep.

payload.title: Why We Ran
paragraphs: The white caravan rolls into the Arkgrave, a gold-hazed fen where Halcyon's ships lie on their sides, far from any sea.
Twelve hundred years ago these Arks fled the city's fall, and the tides threw them here. The crew camps in the shadow of a hull, and nobody says aloud that they are running too.
By the fire the Innkeeper sits down beside the Commander. She has carried a question since tithe day.

payload.title: Still Here
paragraphs: The Hierarch falls, and the organ breaks. The tithe that ran up the spire for twelve hundred years runs nowhere now, and no one will drink the skim again.
You saw your own face in the archive, among the commanders who chose to feed the Lullaby. Halcyon built all of this, and you helped. Today you broke the last of what your people made.
The Manalith does not fall. The Anchors still hold it, as low in the sky as it has ever been, and it is still coming.
But the crew are still here. So are you.

payload.title: Tithe Day
paragraphs: Once there was Halcyon. Its towers burned with light, its Arks rode the tides, and in every hand an orb held a little of the sky.
Halcyon fell in a single night, twelve hundred years ago. The tides rose higher than its towers, its lights went out, and by dawn most of its people were gone.

payload.title: Tithe Day
paragraphs: Above the world, beside the Moon, hangs the Manalith: a vast crusted stone, bristling with crystal, with a faint light leaking out between the cracks. It is not a moon.
The Moon never changes. The Manalith does. Every year it fills a little more of the sky, and every year the Choir has to sing a little harder to keep it asleep.

payload.title: Tithe Day
paragraphs: The song is the Lullaby, and it is paid for. Once a year the Choir's white collectors come for the tithe: a share of the colour, the mana, the life in every person.
Those tithed too hard come back white and empty, and walk behind the caravans. People call them the Hollow.
Twelve hundred years of tithes and hymns, and the world forgot what Halcyon was, and why it fell. The Choir has never wanted it remembered.

payload.title: Tithe Day
paragraphs: Today is tithe day in Saltmoss, on the Tithe Moors. The white caravan waits in the square, and the Captain's militia keep the queue straight.
A handful of ordinary people have decided they will not stand in it. They have nothing left to give and nowhere to run to. They do not know they are heroes yet.
They only know they are going to steal that caravan.

payload.title: Tithe Day
paragraphs: Far from Saltmoss, in a cold tank in the Still, the tithe runs through someone who died the night Halcyon fell.
A heart starts. Eyes open on white walls and cyan light, and nothing is familiar but the weight of an orb in an empty hand.
Wake up, {commander}. You are twelve hundred years late, and by dawn you will be standing in Saltmoss, beside a caravan that is about to be stolen.

payload.title: The Bloom
paragraphs: The reservoir broke, and what the Hierarch stole came down: red blossom through the old white stone, moss over Halcyon's dead. The Manalith is a third larger here than it was over Halcyon, and for the first time, under it, something grows.

Nobody has held the Bloom since the Cathedral fell, so everything that came to feed on it is still here, in the numbers of a place left alone. Redline cuts the blossom to sell. The Choir's last Templars come to burn it. The moss stands up to fight them both.

payload.title: The Choir's Cathedral
paragraphs: At the top of the spire the Choir sings the tithe up into the sky, and takes more than the Manalith needs. The rest fills the organ's pipes, and the Hierarch drinks from them.

The Manalith has never hung so large over anyone's head. The Choir's whole force is waiting, every order of it at once, and the floor above the pipes is already giving way. The spire was Halcyon's before it was theirs. Some of its doors still know you.

payload.title: The Anchor Wastes
paragraphs: North of the last hold the world turns white, and the Anchors stand across it: arches bigger than mountains, humming so low you feel it in your teeth. They are not holding anything up. They are drawing mana down, and the Manalith follows the draw.

It hangs larger every day you walk toward it. The Watch still stands at every arch, long past the time it should have died, and the cold breeds its own. The ice will slide you past where you meant to stop, and the floor will crack, and then it is gone.

payload.title: Under the Anchors
paragraphs: The arches were built on something. Under the Anchors the chains run down into the dark, and the Ember have come to pull every one of them open and bring the Manalith down. Only Halcyon's mana can open or close them. Only you have any left.

When an Anchor heaves, everything near it is dragged a step closer, friend and foe. Chain wardens and hook throwers pull you out of line between heaves. A pincer here closes or breaks by the field, not by your heroes.

payload.title: Halcyon
paragraphs: Out of the Still's back gate the dead towers of Halcyon rise under a pink sky. You knew these streets once. They have been dark for twelve hundred years, and the city's memory went dark with them.

Mana is thinnest here, so close under the Manalith that what lives in the towers has almost nothing of its own. Ghosts, the Hollow, and echoes that mock you by doing what you just did. Above it all the Hierarch's spire drinks.

payload.title: The Underspire
paragraphs: Under the spire, Halcyon is holding its breath. The neon markets of the Underspire still run, on the old taps, and every light kept burning down here draws the Manalith a little closer.

Burrowers and pit lurkers live in the hollows beneath the streets. Shovers push whoever they can toward the holes. The floor cracks under every fight and does not mend. The Street will make you an offer. Count the tiles you are standing on first.

payload.title: The Shardfall
paragraphs: Past the pass the grass gives out and the ground goes red. The first great pieces of the Manalith's shell came down here, and the Choir's walkers still dig at them.

The Manalith hangs a little larger now, and it did not let go of its shell alone. Things fell with it, and they move under the sand. The Ember drink from the red rivers and leave the ground burning behind them. Here, standing still is how you lose.

payload.title: Deep Shardfall
paragraphs: Nobody digs in the deep Shardfall anymore, and nobody guards it. The shell lies thickest here, and the Manalith is still shedding it. The Ember have made this their heartland, and the Captain has followed the money.

The shard callers bring the strikes down on purpose. A piece of sky lands where the timeline says it will, on friend and foe alike. Read it and get clear. Read it well and you can stand them under it.

payload.title: The Tithe Moors
paragraphs: Saltmoss is behind you, and the Choir's white caravan rattles under your crew. Ahead the moors roll grey and green, stone wall after stone wall, and every hold you pass has paid the tithe for longer than it has kept records.

Overhead the Manalith is only a speck, a little larger than the old folk remember. Out here the danger is still the ordinary kind: things gone hungry under it, and the Captain's men on your trail. Stand in the slime and it holds you. Fire lets you go.

payload.title: The Free Holds
paragraphs: The gold hills again, and every gate barred. With the Hierarch gone, the Free Holds have stopped paying the tithe and started building walls. Everyone who wants the empty spire comes here first. So does the Captain, still collecting.

The Manalith hangs larger over the holds than it did over the moors where you started. The wrights throw up fresh walls every wave, and a wall between you and a foe is a pincer you do not get to close. Break them, or go around.

payload.title: The Lantern Road
paragraphs: The moors fall away and the pilgrim road climbs: stone stairs up the gorges, lanterns hung by hands no one will name, shrines painted with skies older than anyone's grandparents.

Look up and the Manalith has hardly moved. What makes the road harder is only the road. The oni hold the passes, and everything else comes fast and from the side, off the cliffs and out of the bamboo. Watch who moves next, or someone will move first.

payload.title: Morrow's Shadow
paragraphs: Past the last road, the Manalith fills the sky. You can count its crystals. The Moon hangs small and steady beside it, the way it always has, the way it did the night you first saw them both.

Its pull lifts the ground and thins the light, and anything more than two tiles from your heroes is lost in the dark. Every danger of the road is here at its worst, and none of it will be seen coming. The Anchors still hold. At the end of this road, the choice is yours.

payload.title: The Still
paragraphs: Every beam off the ice comes down in one place: a white dome at the foot of Halcyon's spire, and above it an oculus that frames the Manalith like a painting. This is the Still. You slept here through the night the city fell. No one else woke.

The Choir fills its tanks with the tithe now. The Hollow stand in its queues, the ones who paid too much, and the Bulwark has mined the floors you have to cross. Choose every step. Some of them are wrong.

payload.title: The Arkgrave
paragraphs: The road west drops into warm fog, and out of it rise the ribs of ships the size of towns. Halcyon built them to outrun the Manalith's pull. The tide brought them here instead, the night the city fell, and they never sailed again.

Nothing burns in the fen. It keeps. Lurkers, shamblers and the dead it has held on to wait among the hulls, and no single fight here is the one that ends you. It is the wet, and the next fight, and the one after that.

payload.title: The Drowned Arks
paragraphs: The Arkgrave again, and the fen is rising. The ships Halcyon built to run from the Manalith are going under at last, row by row, under a sky it fills more of every night.
The tide comes in on a clock. Whoever stands in the water is slowed and shocked, and storm callers ride the flood while drowners come up out of it. There is less ground every wave. Spend it well.
